newsitem.title: ITALY: Uncertainty mars Italy's Enel sale prospect - report.
newsitem.headline: Uncertainty mars Italy's Enel sale prospect - report.

text.p: Uncertainty and controversy over electricity tariffs are likely to weigh on the future privatisation of Italian electricity utility Enel, a report by the Court of Accounts said.

In a report on the utility to parliament, the court, which oversees state accounts, said: "The uncertainties and controversies over tariffs do not allow secure profit forecasts and make the prospect of selling public stakes through placement of...shares on the market uncertain."
According to a government decree law issued in July, it will be up to an energy sector authority yet to be created to fix electricity tariffs by June 30, 1997.
In the meantime the industry ministry will update pricing where necessary.
The court report criticised the fact that complex tariff issues were regulated provisionally by short term solutions, in themselves conditioned by the decree law.

A Senate or upper house of parliament industry committee held up approval of the regulatory body for the energy sector in July when two parties supporting the centre-left government voted against the legislation.

Creation of the authority is vital for the planned privatisation of Enel, now expected to start in the spring of 1997. The draft legislation to create the watchdog is due to be put to a second vote this month.
